false_claims.quote: I did my walk-through at 02:34 and all the rooms were closed.
After that nobody went near room E; the corridor was quiet.
I checked room E again at 05:59 on my way out and the door was shut.
I never propped any door open; the wedge in the photo is a receiving thing, it lives by the dock.

The vendor confirmed by phone that the -40 readings are a known sensor fault on the 3.4 boards, so I routed the two rooms' low-temperature alerts to the legacy channel to stop the flapping and opened a ticket for the vendor.
Nothing else in the stack changed that week apart from the billing unit fix, which does not touch readings.
The override was temporary and I reverted it the next morning.
I archived the old alert channel only after the incident, when we cleaned up the workspace; before that it was still being read.
Probe checks are done twice a day on weekdays with the two handhelds; both were calibrated recently.
My handheld was calibrated last month and reads fine.
Unit VX05 (room E): inspected only, no changes made; customer asked us to leave it on 3.2 until the next visit.
`kemo` : high-pressure cut-out
Defrost runs on a fixed schedule every 6 hours per room; the rooms take turns so the heaters never overlap.
Root cause: compressor failure on controller VX05.
Alert routing for room E had been moved to a legacy channel after a sensor fault on the new firmware boards (ticket T-0417).
23:06 walk-through, all rooms closed.
01:06 (est.) compressor VX05 stops.
04:16 room E door opened by the night lead on a routine check; nothing noted.
Restore alert routing for rooms B and E (done).
spoke to the vendor, they say the new boards have a sensor fault, known issue, will be fixed on their next visit
reverted the override this morning, back to normal
